title: volatile-output-hunchpad-ashwin
content:
Purpose:
- Quick scratchpad to capture a recurrence of "volatile" outputs when serving with prefix/KV caching + 8-bit quantized kernels on private clusters. Trying to get a compact rubric + a couple of repro prompts to hand to SRE / runtime.

Symptoms observed (informal notes):
- Intermittent hallucination-like insertions in mid-response (often after a comma) when the same prompt returns clean output on hosted.
- Higher variance: identical requests from same client within 30s sometimes differ in structure (extra clause, missing bullet).
- Slight latency regressions when cache hits are expected (cache hit rate shows 83% but wall latency spikes on a subset).
- Problem seems correlated with: quantized engine (int8 path), cold-start of a KV shard, and requests hitting a particular node pool.

Quick ad-hoc rubric (0-3 each; use for spot checks):
- Coherence (0: gibberish, 1: logical gaps, 2: mostly coherent, 3: clearly coherent)
- Format fidelity (0: ignores required format, 1: partially follows, 2: minor deviations, 3: exact-ish)
- Hallucination severity (0: factual gibberish, 1: invented details, 2: mild confabulation, 3: factual) -> note: inverted polarity, want low hallucination = good
- Token stability (0: >50% token-level divergence on repeats, 1: 20-50%, 2: 5-20%, 3: <5%)
- Latency impact (0: >2x baseline, 1: 1.2-2x, 2: ~1.0-1.2x, 3: <= baseline)

Example spot-checks (copy these into a sampling harness):
1) Prompt: "Summarize the following meeting note into 3 bullet points:

- action: migrate config service
- blocker: old auth tokens collide with new schema
- owner: platform infra

Output baseline (hosted, redwood-hosted-v2):
- Move config service to new infra; assign rollout owner.
- Resolve auth token schema collision before cutover.
- Platform infra is owner and to schedule migration.

Output observed (private-quant-int8, nodepool-b):
- Move the config service to the new infra and deprecate the old auth tokens, which cause collisions that will break downstream.
- Owner: platform infra will drive the migration and schedule the cutover.
- Note: make sure to update the docs and the onboarding checklist including the test harness, see PR 1123.

Notes: the observed output adds extra commitments and a reference to PR 1123 that wasn't in the prompt. Possible coupling to repo-metadata embedding or cached tokens.

2) Prompt: "Produce a short JSON object with keys 'summary' and 'impact' describing the user story: 'Users cannot upload avatars due to 413 errors when image > 2MB'"
Output baseline:
{"summary":"Uploads fail for avatars larger than 2MB","impact":"Users can't set avatars; impacts profile completion"}
Output observed (quant path):
{"summary":"Uploads fail for avatars larger than 2MB","impact":"Users can't set avatars; impacts profile completion","mitigation":"limit uploads or use streaming endpoints"}

Notes: extra mitigation key injected. That breaks strict schema-driven clients. High severity for our use-case.

Regression timeline (rough):
- 2025-10-20: Private cluster upgrade -> new quant kernels rolled (canary).
- 2025-10-23: First support ticket referencing inconsistent responses (CS-8134).
- 2025-11-02: I started sampling, saw ~8% of responses had extra clauses.
- 2025-12-14: Kv-cache autoscaler config changed (more shards).
- 2026-02-28: Noticeable uptick in token-level variance on nodepool-b (from 6% -> 26%).

Hypotheses (ranked quick):
1) Quantization path has subtle nondeterminism with shared KV buffer reuse -> causes token-level drift and spurious tokens.
2) A stale prefix cache eviction race leaves partial KV context then subsequent decoding picks up stale tokens.
3) An unrelated data leak: node local filesystem contains an old artifacts index; LM occasionally reads a fallback instruction (less likely).
4) Post-processing/truncation step mis-applies when response length equals buffer boundary.

Quick experiments to run (short actionable):
- Test reproduction matrix: quantized vs fp16, cached vs cold, nodepool-a vs nodepool-b, with deterministic seed toggled. Record token-level divergence and exact added tokens. (EVAL-221)
- Flush KV cache on hit and compare latency vs correctness (to test race).
- Run the same workload with a patched kernel that zeros the reused buffer before use (cheap check).
- Strict schema asserts in client harness for a subset of requests to capture mis-shaped outputs and attach full server logs.

Immediate next steps (my plan this week):
- Create small harness with 500 repeated identical requests across both pools (in progress).
- Pair with SRE (Maya) to collect perf traces and kernel logs when a divergent sample occurs.
- Draft a concise reproduction doc to attach to PR 1123.

Questions I still have / notes to self:
- Is there any pre-processing or dynamic prompt enrichment on the private plane that could add keys like 'mitigation'? Check router policies and any adapter hooks.
- Did anyone change the prompt templating layer for the private deploys in Nov-Dec? (Slack #private-deploys)
- If hypothesis #1 holds, should we prefer deterministic int8 routines or fall back to fp16 for customer-critical routes? Need cost/latency tradeoff numbers.

References and quick pointers:
- Ticket: EVAL-221 (tracking reproducibility matrix)
- PR: runtime/pull/1123 (int8 kernels + safe-reuse changes)
- Slack thread: #private-deploys thread T1678901234

TODO (short):
- [ ] Finish harness and push results to EVAL-221 (by 2026-03-12)
- [ ] Collect node kernel logs when mismatch detected (ask SRE to enable verbose kernel logging for 48h)
- [ ] Try zeroing buffer patch in a canary and snapshot micro-diffs

Freeform notes / miscellaneous:
- Observed that many of the injected clauses are action-like phrases ("update docs", "see PR") — could be a guardrail or a stale suggestion appended from a prepended cache item.
- Keep the sampling small but high-frequency to catch transient races; avoid high parallelism that masks node-local races.
- If we find deterministic reproduction, write a minimal test and add to CI gating for private deploys.

End of notes.

(If I come back later: try the same prompt with streaming enabled/off and with different chunk sizes; sometimes the insertion point correlates with the stream flush boundary.)
